messages.content: How do I find the angle of the force for a given momentum?

function.name: calculate_vector_angle
function.description: Calculate the angle of a vector based on its X and Y components. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

X_component.description: The X component of the vector. This is a float type value.

Y_component.description: The Y component of the vector. This is a float type value.

use_degrees.description: If true, the result will be in degrees. If false, the result will be in radians. Default is false.

message.content:
To determine the direction (angle) of a force vector, you need its horizontal (X) and vertical (Y) components.  
Once you have those, the angle θ relative to the positive X‑axis is given by  

\[
θ = \operatorname{atan2}(Y_{\text{component}},\, X_{\text{component}})
\]

(Use `atan2` instead of `atan` so the sign of both components is taken into account and the angle is placed in the correct quadrant.)

If you’d like me to compute the angle for a specific force, please provide the X and Y components of that force (or of the momentum change that gives the force). Once I have those numbers, I can call the helper function to give you the angle in degrees or radians.
